title: Fixed Three Aisle And Apsidal Hall Section
description: One newly authored complete static architectural section of a high central longitudinal hall, two lower side aisles and a semicircular rear chamber. Two complete parallel high arcade assemblies have three genuine ground-to-arch openings each, connecting the central floor to lower lateral passages. Whole side walls and inclined aisle roofs sit below the retained high central gabled roof. A single continuous floor expands into the rear semicircular chamber, whose thick half-cylinder wall and closed thick half-dome terminate only the central hall, not all three aisles. The front half of the high roof and the front-right low roof/wall are deliberately omitted as finite presentation sections to expose the interior hierarchy; all retained pieces have closed finite edges. Unlike the earlier monitor roof alone, this includes grounded rooms, arcades, lower aisles and an apsidal termination; unlike a square groin bay it is a longitudinal three-volume organization rather than crossed cylindrical roofs. All coordinates newly authored, no old columns, roof or church parts imported. Three opaque solid PBR appearances, metres Z-up and bounds-centred ground datum, one static architecture model zero scenes. A generic artistic sectional building, not a historically exact basilica or a religious-use proposal. No people, rituals, furnishing, hidden finished front facade, complete weather enclosure, occupancy, daylight, acoustics, load, construction, historical accuracy, building-code or safety capability. No rigging animation interaction.
